notes: If a woman in labor lacks strength to bring forth her baby, both mother and child are in danger of death. The day of reckoning has arrived for Hezekiah and his armies, and he realizes they don't have strength in themselves to be victorious over their enemies.
servants (na'ar) literally, "youths," mere lads, implying belittling

quotes.text: The word rumour as used here does not mean the report will be false or incorrect. The sense of the sentence is that the king of Assyria will hear (receive) news from home that will cause him to return.
quotes.speaker: Daniel H. Ludlow
quotes.source: A Companion to Your Study of the Old Testament
quotes.attr: Daniel H. Ludlow, A Companion to Your Study of the Old Testament, 299

notes: Egypt was in part governed by three successive Ethiopian monarchs, for forty or fifty years: Sabacho, Sevechus, and Tirhakah.

Gozan a district in Mesopotamia Haran--more to the west. Abraham removed to it from Ur (Ge 11:31) Rezeph--farther west, in Syria. Eden--There is an ancient village, Adna, north of Baghdad. Telassar--now Tel-afer, west of Mosul
Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah (cities in Babylon) The kings of these lands received no support from their gods and were removed from their thrones by Assyria's kings.
ear . . . eyes--singular, plural. In Hebrew when we wish to hear a thing we lend one ear; when we wish to see a thing we open both eyes.

The policy of the Assyrians in order to alienate the conquered peoples from their own countries was, both to deport them elsewhere, and to destroy the tutelary idols of their nation, the strongest tie which bound them to their native land. The Roman policy was just the reverse.
The strongest argument to plead before God in prayer, the honor of God (Ex 32:12-14; Ps 83:18; Da 9:18, 19).

virgin . . . daughter of Zion. These are metaphors for Jerusalem (1:8; 3:16). ). "Virgin" implies that the city is, as yet, inviolate. "Daughter" is the population, the child of the place (see on Isa 23:10; Isa 1:8). For example - Zion and her inhabitants.

quotes.text: I have digged, and drunk water/I dried up all the Nile of Egypt. Sennacherib boasts of his power to produce water-or to dry it up, symbolizing his confidence in his ability to conquer Egypt. As one commentator notes, "The king's foot is equal to blocking even the Nile itself!

notes: In other words …Thou dost boast that it is all by thy counsel and might: but it is I who, long ago, have ordered it so (Isa 22:11); thou wert but the instrument in My hands (Isa 10:5, 15). This was the reason why "the inhabitants were of small power before thee" (Isa 37:27), namely, that I ordered it so; yet thou art in My hands, and I know thy ways (Isa 37:28), and I will check thee (Isa 37:29).
before it be grown up ["The cornfield (frail and tender), before the corn is grown."]

Like a wild beast led by a ring through the nose, he shall be forced back to his own country (compare Job 41:1, 2; Eze 19:4; 29:4; 38:4). In a bas-relief of Khorsabad, captives are led before the king by a cord attached to a hook, or ring, passing through the under lip or the upper lip, and nose.
The sign is that in the third year Sennacherib will leave quickly
JST adds the words in italics: "and they that escape out of Jerusalem shall come up upon mount Zion."

quotes.text: The "remnant" that went forth "out of Jerusalem" at the time of the Assyrian siege of Jerusalem could have been one of the "graftings" mentioned by the prophet Zenos as recorded in the Book of Mormon. (See Jacob 5:8, 13, 14, 20-28)
